source_text: Paulus servus Jesu Christi, vocatus apostolus, segregatus in Evangelium Dei. Vocatus non est idem quod electus — multi vocati, pauci electi. Segregatus in Evangelium: Deus segregat iustos a ventre; Paulus non fortuito sed secundum propositum vocatus est.
thought_title: Paul's calling and separation for the gospel
orientation: Origen is explaining the opening words of Romans, where Paul describes himself as servant, called apostle, and set apart for the gospel.
pass_a_gloss: Paul [a] servant of Jesus Christ, called [an] apostle, separated into [the] Gospel of God. Called not is [the] same [thing] that chosen — many called, few chosen. Separated into [the] Gospel: God separates [the] just from [the] womb; Paul not by chance but according to [the] purpose called is.

choices.english: set apart for the gospel of God
choices.why: The glossary does not cover this phrase, but 'set apart' preserves the literal sense of segregatus as separation for a purpose, matching the source's spatial metaphor.
rejected: separated unto the gospel of God
segregated for the gospel of God

choices.term: vocatus non est idem quod electus
choices.english: Called is not the same thing as chosen
choices.why: The source explicitly distinguishes vocatus from electus; 'chosen' is the standard English for electus and keeps the contrast sharp.

choices.english: many are called, few are chosen
choices.why: This is a recognizable biblical saying; the literal rendering preserves the parallel structure and the contrast between calling and election.
rejected: many are invited, few are selected

choices.english: God sets apart the righteous from the womb
choices.why: The phrase 'from the womb' is literal and echoes biblical language about God's prior separation of the righteous; 'sets apart' keeps the same verb as the earlier clause.
rejected: God separates the just from the womb
God sets aside the righteous from birth

choices.english: not by chance but according to purpose
choices.why: The contrast between fortuito and propositum is central to Origen's argument against heretics; 'by chance' and 'according to purpose' preserve the exact opposition.
rejected: not randomly but according to plan

bible_refs.note: Paulus servus Jesu Christi, vocatus apostolus, segregatus in Evangelium Dei

pass_b_english: "Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God" (Romans 1:1). Called is not the same thing as chosen, for "many are called, but few are chosen" (Matthew 22:14). Set apart for the gospel: God sets apart the righteous from the womb. Paul was called not by chance but according to purpose.

last_rejected.fix: Called is not the same thing as elect, for 'many are called, but few are elect'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Chosen' is within normal semantic range of 'electus'; glossary consistency is a preference, not a major error.

last_rejected.fix: many are called, but few are elect
last_rejected.ruling: 'Chosen' correctly renders 'electi' here; glossary preference for 'elect' does not change meaning or mislead.
